desc:
Count the different strings that occur in s as a substring exactly once (overlapping occurrences count as separate occurrences). A string that occurs twice or more is not counted at all, and each qualifying string is counted a single time.

s = "abab"  ->  4   ("aba", "bab", "abab", "ba")
s = "aaaa"  ->  1   ("aaaa"; "aaa" occurs twice, and so on)
s = "abc"   ->  6   (every substring is unique)
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
The answer is at most n(n+1)/2 and fits in 32 bits
hints: Put every substring in a counter and count entries with value 1. How big does the counter get?
A substring that occurs once corresponds to exactly one suffix, and it is a prefix of that suffix that is longer than the suffix's common prefix with the neighbours in sorted order.
With the sorted suffixes and the neighbour LCP array, suffix k of length len contributes max(0, len - max(lcp[k-1], lcp[k])) unique substrings. Sum these contributions.
editorial: A substring that occurs exactly once starts at exactly one position, so it is a prefix of exactly one suffix. Sort the suffixes; the suffixes sharing a prefix are contiguous, so prefix length L of suffix k is shared with another suffix if and only if L ≤ max(lcp[k-1], lcp[k]). All longer prefixes of this suffix are unique, and no two different suffixes can produce the same unique string.

So the answer is sum over k of max(0, (n - sa[k]) - max(lcp[k-1], lcp[k])). The max with 0 handles a suffix that is itself a prefix of a neighbour (then every prefix is repeated). Total time O(n log2 n) with prefix-doubling suffix array construction, plus O(n) for Kasai's LCP and the sum. Counting with a hash map is O(n3) character work.
